analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. The patch excerpt is complete and shows two edits. The first bumps the 'Last updated' date from 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-13 (head line 3). The second adds a documentation paragraph near base line 2192 / head lines 2192-2197 about run-isolation regression tests for the CI route-label planner. It covers the request header, exact run-qualified Linux and Mac labels, fallback for generic or other-run responses, and incompatible label sets across runs. The paragraph explicitly claims no live runner or VM test.

The supplied units are base lines 3188-3653 and head lines 1-450. They contain only descriptive test documentation. The added paragraph near head 2192 is not in any supplied unit, but the patch excerpt shows it in full. Nothing executable, no configuration and no code changed, so the change adds no new attack surface. It does not touch the provider wire protocol (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041, TB-007), key custody or the fan helper (TB-010). It adds no secrets, tokens or credentials.

The surrounding text mentions SSD test volumes, cluster tests and the prefix-cache encoding. It documents existing test behavior and is unchanged. The new text describes CI job-label isolation, which is CI infrastructure outside the provider threat model's scope. I could not verify that the described tests or the CI route-label implementation exist or behave as documented, because they are not in the supplied evidence. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated, and no threat-model update is needed.
